clauses.required_clause: Show QuickLRU as the controller owning the current and old in-memory maps, the current-generation count, maxSize and optional expiry policy; do not imply persistent or remote storage.
clauses.observed: The controller, Current Map, Old Map, count, and in-memory-only boundary are explicit; the rotation label also names maxSize. The graphic calls an Expiry guard but never identifies the instance's optional maxAge/expiry policy or that it derives from the constructor option.
clauses.reason: The missing optional expiry-policy state leaves a required ownership/policy fact unshown. No persistent or remote storage is implied.

clauses.required_clause: Show set for a current-generation key versus a key absent from the current generation (possibly still in the old generation), and generation rotation at the configured threshold; distinguish rotation from evicting just the one least-recent item.
clauses.observed: The diagram shows current-key replacement, an absent-current add/increment branch, count >= maxSize, whole-map swap, prior-old callback, and a card correctly saying the rotation code does not select one least-recent item. It does not show or say that the absent-current branch can still have an old-generation entry; set only tests #cache and then inserts into it.
clauses.reason: The requested old-generation possibility is material to the distinction and is absent, although the displayed threshold rotation is source-entailing.

clauses.required_clause: Show get from the current generation, get/promotion from the old generation and a missing key. Preserve the actual expiry checks and their effect on removal/return.
clauses.observed: Current and old hits, old-key deletion followed by #set promotion, and missing-or-expired undefined are shown. The Expiry guard only says 'check an expiring item' and 'expired item: notify, then delete(key)'; it omits the actual predicate (numeric expiry at or before Date.now()) and the current-hit versus old-hit return paths after that check.
clauses.reason: A generic expiry box does not preserve the required actual check, even though its deletion/callback effect is correctly summarized.

clauses.required_clause: Explain that has and peek inspect without get-style promotion, including their expiry behavior.
clauses.observed: The inspection node and card correctly state current-then-old inspection with no promotion, and its edge reaches the generic Expiry guard. The diagram does not distinguish expired has returning false from expired peek returning undefined after deletion.
clauses.reason: The required expiry behavior for both inspection methods is not fully explained.

clauses.required_clause: Distinguish onEviction for expired/rotated-out entries from explicit delete and clear. Show their effects on both maps/current count without inventing callbacks on manual deletion.
clauses.observed: Expiry and rotation connect to onEviction; delete/clear connect to both maps and state count adjustment/reset. The amber card explicitly says public delete and clear do not invoke onEviction.
clauses.reason: The displayed callback boundaries and state effects entail the pinned implementation.

clauses.required_clause: Iteration, resize and exact public size arithmetic are outside scope. Support all authored claims with inspected source ranges; include useful views/cards without content-count targets.
clauses.observed: Iteration, resize, and public size arithmetic are absent. Component metadata supplies relevant index.js ranges, and the cards' rotation, promotion, expiry, and manual-removal claims are entailed by those ranges. Three focused views and three explanatory cards are useful rather than quota-driven.
clauses.reason: The checked authored claims have supporting inspected source ranges in the specification metadata.

supported_claims: Rotation emits every prior-old entry, then replaces old with current and starts a fresh current Map at count 0 (index.js:68-77).
An unexpired old get deletes the old key and reinserts it through #set (index.js:80-83, 111-115).
Expired access calls onEviction when supplied and then public delete(key) (index.js:40-49).
Public delete and clear do not call onEviction (index.js:166-179).
unsupported_or_incomplete_display_claims: The generic expiry wording does not state the source predicate: typeof item.expiry === 'number' && item.expiry <= Date.now() (index.js:40-41).
The inspection wording does not state has=false versus peek=undefined for expired entries (index.js:137-157, 52-65).
The absent-current set route does not communicate that #oldCache is not tested by set (index.js:125-132).
citation_entailment.note: Source references are present in diagram metadata; captures show SRC badges but not expanded path/range text.

observations: All diagram nodes, boundary, callback, legend, and controls are contained in each 1440x900 and 2048x1320 light/dark capture.
At 1440x900 the cards continue below the viewport; this is normal vertical Reader-document scrolling and not clipping.
At 2048x1320, all three cards are visible and readable in both themes.

At 1440x900, major node titles remain readable, but many connection labels and node sublabels are very small; in dark mode the muted blue/gray route labels have weak contrast against the grid. This makes several semantic distinctions difficult to read at the common viewport without zooming.

overall_reason: The artifact accurately depicts rotation, promotion, callback boundaries, and manual removal, but it does not fully satisfy four required semantic clauses: optional expiry policy, the old-generation possibility during set, the actual expiry predicate/return effects for get, and distinct expired has/peek results. The 1440px dark capture also leaves fine route text insufficiently legible.
